There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Tom always says that small steps matter more than big plans. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. Also, a wobbly wheel slowed the trolley.

There are always more possibilities than we expect. Little by little, things began to change. The school clinic has become an important part of daily life. For example, the nurse offered a mild sedative before the scan.

Mia ordered bread and coffee at the school clinic last night. People around Mia often share different ideas about the dining hall. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. She cut her finger on the knife.

Mia thanked Tom for the honest advice. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The dining hall looked quieter than usual that evening. Best of all, an eye test is free for kids.
Mia's dream job is to be a cook. The experience taught Mia more than any book could. Mia is saving money to buy a ticket to Chengdu.
